{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible with single-column ELM ensemble; snow physics and SWE are core ELM capabilities. SNOTEL-based validation is possible but requires the user to supply/ingest observed SWE separately since ELM does not read SNOTEL directly.",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulated peak (maximum annual) SWE at each elevation band along the Wenatchee gradient",
      "Timing of peak SWE and melt-out date per column",
      "Elevation-dependent SWE gradient (SWE vs. elevation lapse)",
      "Model vs. SNOTEL bias/RMSE at co-located points if observed SWE is provided offline"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Basin-integrated snow volume or spatially distributed snowpack (single-column, no lateral routing)",
      "Wind redistribution / avalanche / drift processes not represented in ELM",
      "Sub-grid canopy-gap snow heterogeneity beyond ELM's single-column parameterization",
      "Direct automated SNOTEL retrieval/scoring inside ELM (validation is a post-processing step)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "Five single columns are placed at real SNOTEL locations spanning the Wenatchee basin elevation gradient (~1035 m to ~1875 m) so that simulated peak SWE can be compared point-by-point against long-term SNOTEL SWE records and the elevation dependence of peak SWE can be resolved.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "fish_lake_1036m", "lat": 47.5533, "lon": -120.8722, "soil_texture": "gravelly sandy loam"},
    {"id": "trinity_1451m", "lat": 47.9928, "lon": -120.9925, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "stevens_pass_1238m", "lat": 47.7325, "lon": -121.0872, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "pope_ridge_1338m", "lat": 47.7864, "lon": -120.7269, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "lyman_lake_1798m", "lat": 48.1611, "lon": -120.9019, "soil_texture": "loamy sand (thin alpine soil over bedrock)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1991",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2020",
    "STOP_N": "30",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1991-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOWDP",
      "SNOW_DEPTH",
      "FSNO",
      "QFLX_SNOW_MELT",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "QSNOFRZ",
      "SNOWLIQ",
      "SNOWICE",
      "SNOW",
      "RAIN",
      "TSA",
      "TSOI",
      "FSDS",
      "FLDS",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-point/single-column mode (PTS_MODE) with site-specific surface datasets",
    "Elevation-appropriate atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or downscaled/lapse-adjusted reanalysis) per column",
    "ELM snow model (multi-layer snowpack, SNICAR albedo) enabled",
    "Post-processing/validation workflow to align model output with SNOTEL daily SWE observations"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_N interpreted in years (STOP_OPTION=nyears) run after a spin-up sufficient to equilibrate soil/hydrology",
    "Peak SWE defined as maximum daily H2OSNO in each water year (Oct 1 - Sep 30)",
    "Forcing air temperature and precipitation are lapse-rate corrected to each column elevation since default GSWP3 grid is coarse relative to the Cascade terrain",
    "Column locations correspond to established NRCS SNOTEL stations in/near the Wenatchee River basin for direct observational comparison",
    "SNOTEL observed SWE time series are obtained externally and regridded to model daily output for bias/RMSE/correlation scoring",
    "Land cover set to evergreen needleleaf forest for mid-elevation sites and to sparse alpine/barren for the highest site consistent with observed vegetation"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible with single-column ELM ensemble; snow physics and SWE are core ELM capabilities. SNOTEL-based validation is possible but requires the user to supply/ingest observed SWE separately since ELM does not read SNOTEL directly.
answerable: Simulated peak (maximum annual) SWE at each elevation band along the Wenatchee gradient
Timing of peak SWE and melt-out date per column
Elevation-dependent SWE gradient (SWE vs. elevation lapse)
Model vs. SNOTEL bias/RMSE at co-located points if observed SWE is provided offline
not_answerable: Basin-integrated snow volume or spatially distributed snowpack (single-column, no lateral routing)
Wind redistribution / avalanche / drift processes not represented in ELM
Sub-grid canopy-gap snow heterogeneity beyond ELM's single-column parameterization
Direct automated SNOTEL retrieval/scoring inside ELM (validation is a post-processing step)

parsed.n_justification: Five single columns are placed at real SNOTEL locations spanning the Wenatchee basin elevation gradient (~1035 m to ~1875 m) so that simulated peak SWE can be compared point-by-point against long-term SNOTEL SWE records and the elevation dependence of peak SWE can be resolved.

columns.soil_texture: loamy sand (thin alpine soil over bedrock)

requires_capabilities: ELM single-point/single-column mode (PTS_MODE) with site-specific surface datasets
Elevation-appropriate atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or downscaled/lapse-adjusted reanalysis) per column
ELM snow model (multi-layer snowpack, SNICAR albedo) enabled
Post-processing/validation workflow to align model output with SNOTEL daily SWE observations
assumptions: STOP_N interpreted in years (STOP_OPTION=nyears) run after a spin-up sufficient to equilibrate soil/hydrology
Peak SWE defined as maximum daily H2OSNO in each water year (Oct 1 - Sep 30)
Forcing air temperature and precipitation are lapse-rate corrected to each column elevation since default GSWP3 grid is coarse relative to the Cascade terrain
Column locations correspond to established NRCS SNOTEL stations in/near the Wenatchee River basin for direct observational comparison
SNOTEL observed SWE time series are obtained externally and regridded to model daily output for bias/RMSE/correlation scoring
Land cover set to evergreen needleleaf forest for mid-elevation sites and to sparse alpine/barren for the highest site consistent with observed vegetation
